column8: Mon 16 Nov: 2.2, the date the hole was made, for the one clause SKELETON allows; Fisher's two quotes re-read at source today (PO-749, 31 Oct 2001), word for word; known to bond readers, so rarity 3.

Mon 16 Nov: store, with at most half a clause in 2.2: the bond was stopped for need and relevance, not safety; quotes re-read at PO-749 today; the report needs the date and the forecast (rows 1, 3), not the reasons.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.2 or 3e, the cause was a forecast, which sets up the contrast with TNA l.15 (not merely a forecast); Fisher's surplus case re-read at source; the CRS debt-retirement point is the fetch tool's paraphrase, so quote only discontinued in November 2001.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.2 wording guard: say expecting surpluses to return, never when it ran budget surpluses; the deficit and September 11th quotes re-read at PO-749 today; pairs with row 3 and keeps row 27's clause true.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.2, the failed half of a failed forecast, needed if the clause says the forecast failed; keep its own guard, never surpluses never returned (fiscal years not read); the Feb 2006 return checked in auction data today.

Mon 16 Nov: store or Table 1 note: the hole's left edge, the 5-3/8% Feb-2031 bond, last sold 9 Aug 2001 ($5bn, 5.520%); auction records re-read today; $16.4bn outstanding matches MSPD; serves no part beyond the edge date.

Mon 16 Nov: guard for row 27's wording (the Apr 2032 TIPS is the one bond inside the hole, auction of 10 Oct 2001 checked today); fix: the next TIPS outstanding matures in 2040 is false, ten-year TIPS mature all through 2032-2036 (row 11's 12), so say the next 30-year TIPS; never offered for Laura (banned).

Mon 16 Nov: 2.2, the hole's right edge is the bond Caplet chose IBTR over for 2037, which links the history to the one real choice; 9 Feb 2006, 4-1/2%, $14bn at 4.530% and the Aug 2006 reopening checked in auction data today; never say it failed a price check (Q29-011).

Mon 16 Nov: twin of row 10, the same hole shown in auction records (22 records and the nominal maturities re-read today, all match); row 10 shows it in today's outstanding debt, which is what WInS could list; carry this row's maturity list with it.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.2 and Table 1 note: no nominal bond outstanding matures between 15 Feb 2031 and 15 Feb 2036 (recounted today in the MSPD repo copy: 113 bonds, none in the window; edges $16.4bn and $26.4bn), the fact the one clause rests on.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.2 and 3e wording guard against a judge who knows the market: 57 notes and 12 TIPS mature inside the window (recounted today: 57 notes, about $4.48 trillion; per-year counts match), so write no Treasury bond, never no Treasuries; TNA l.15 stays true as a statement about WInS's list.

Mon 16 Nov: store, 3e at most: the four notes and coupons checked in MSPD today; Wharton's 6 Oct rule limits Laura to WInS-listed securities, so never offer these notes as her option; useful only to say what a WInS-free adviser would have bought.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.2, the forced funds hold Treasury notes of exactly those years (recounted today: IBTM 15, IBTO 11, IBTP 4, IBTQ 4, all 91282C; IBTM's latest 30 Nov 2032), so the funds are not a second-best issuer; say held for her at one remove; payout stays a net asset value (TNA l.15), never fixed.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.2's one real choice and what it shows: IBTR held the Feb-2036 bond itself (912810FT0 at 3.03% on 24 Sep, checked in the repo snapshot), so the choice was never distrust of that bond; say IBTR holds a slice of it, never that the 2037 payment rests on it; the wrapper-and-date reading is Keel's, not Caplet's stated reason (CANON D13); re-read holdings before 27 Nov.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.2, sorts history's constraint from the simulator's, which row 27's clause needs; the WInS half is the team's record plus inference (WInS off limits), the history half checked in MSPD; one clause at most, as SKELETON's cut list says.

Mon 16 Nov: store: the unlisted May-2037 and Nov-2040 bonds are in the team record (trading_notes.csv, checked 5 Oct) and 113 outstanding matches MSPD; SKELETON 2.2 allows one clause on WInS's list, so the simulator's own gaps stay out of the report beyond TNA l.5.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.2 guard: the 20-year's absence (last sold 8 Jan 1986, back 20 May 2020; both checked in auction data today) is the other cause of the hole, so the clause never says 2001 alone decided it; 1981-86 sales were roughly quarterly (1982 had a gap).
Mon 16 Nov: a sourcing guard that travels with row 17: date the 20-year's end from Treasury auction data (8 Jan 1986, re-read today), never from the CRS line; no part needs it on its own.

Mon 16 Nov: store or Table 1 note: explains Q38-012's twin-coupon dates (1.375% Nov 2040 and 2.000% Nov 2041 are 20-year bonds of 2020-21, checked in auction data today); WInS listing of the Nov-2041 twin is not in the team record; adds a reason, not a new fact.

Mon 16 Nov: store, 2.2 only as would likely have: four skipped years, one bond per forced payment, matches the cold reader's count (five payments rest on funds, four forced); a Keel counterfactual: the Feb 2000 new bond matured in May 2030, so the February dates are an assumption.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.2's each forced constraint joined to its price, but no figure and a gap in the logic: Caplet chose a fund over a par bond for 2037, so the hole may have cost nothing the team valued; say so, use NUMBERS 8m's about 17 days (not two weeks) and NUMBERS 3 for any payout figure; the funds pay net asset value, never fixed.

Mon 16 Nov: store only; fix: 2007 auctions were quarterly (Feb, May, Aug, Nov; checked today), not semi-annual, and the calendar also made the 5% May-2037 bond, so the 10.5-month wait traces to WInS's list, not the auction calendar; SKELETON cuts the 10.5-month wait from 2.5 (Trading Note 1 says it).

Mon 16 Nov: the parallel breaks under its own disanalogy: the TBAC minutes (row 24) say the bond came back though not necessary to meet expected financing needs, so the named exit was not what brought it back; set beside IPS l.17's two reasons it teaches the reverse lesson, that rules get changed outside their exits; quotes verified, keep them in row 24's store home.

Mon 16 Nov: store: the Treasury's long-bond calendar serves its own funding, so Laura takes WInS's list as she finds it; soften never a buyer's (the minutes cite a wider investor base); minutes of an advisory committee, not a Treasury decision, said so if quoted.

Mon 16 Nov: store only; fix the use: CRS argued long-liability investors would benefit from a new 30-year (duration supply), not that they met a 2031-2036 maturity hole, so never write liability-matched savers met this hole before Laura; serves no part as worded.

Mon 16 Nov: twin of row 7 (TIPS, store only, banned for Laura) with the same error: ten-year TIPS mature all through 2032-2036, so the jump to 2040 is for 30-year TIPS only; Fisher's inflation-adjusted quote re-read at PO-749 today travels with row 7.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.2's one clause and a candidate for the open aha slot (a WInS quirk is a 2001 forecast); fix: none exists is false for the 3-3/8% Apr 2032 TIPS, so say no ordinary Treasury bond matures then; say Caplet chose IBTR over the Feb-2036 bond, not passed over; any count says five payments rest on funds, four forced; name the 20-year's absence (row 17) or avoid implying 2001 alone; test cold first.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.2 wording guard; fix per tonight's cold reader: five payments rest on funds (IBTM to IBTR, 2033-2037), four forced (2033-2036) and one chosen (2037), so ban four payments rest on funds and five forced, never five payments itself; keep the other three bans; a forecast did is half the cause (row 17).

Mon 16 Nov: conceit owner only, 2.2 has no V2.2 turn yet; pencil covers every forecast (CONCEIT V2.1), but the cancelled auctions left a permanent hole, so the image runs both ways and must say the forecast was rubbed out while the hole stayed; same-field parallel, not strikingly dissimilar; reader test before use, never in Table 1.

Mon 16 Nov: coherence guard for 2.2: the finding changes no holding or figure (NUMBERS l.65 frozen instruments; IPS l.13 and TNA l.15 stand); 2.2 evaluates the forced choices, never repeats them; a check, not an idea.
